# iliad-072 — renderings chosen for 12.1–87 (to be copied into conventions.md)

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| ὁμιλαδόν (12.3) | "in a throng" | "in a throng" | "in crowds", "in masses", "in bands"; ὅμιλος "throng" (the table's 4.209 row) with the adverb ending -δόν |
| ἰάομαι (ἰᾶτ’ Εὐρύπυλον βεβλημένον, 12.2) | "was healing Eurypylus, struck" | "healing the wounded Eurypylus" | "treating", "doctoring"; βεβλημένος "struck" / "wounded" as in iliad-071 |
| ἔμελλε + inf. (12.3–4, 12.34) | "was destined … to hold out" · "were destined … to bring it about" | "as it turned out, was no longer going to hold out" · "were to bring it about" | "was bound to", "would not", "as it proved" (the table says "as it turned out", 5.205); ἔμελλον "destined" in `l` (the table's 5.686 row), "was going to" in `i` |
| σχήσειν (absolute, 12.4) | "to hold out" | "to hold out" | "to hold", "to last", "to stand"; ἔχω with no object, taken as "hold out" |
| ὕπερθεν … τεῖχος εὐρύ (12.4–5) | "the wall above it, wide" | "the wide wall above it" | "the wall on top" (drops the ditch), "broad"; εὐρύς "wide" |
| ὄφρά σφιν … ῥύοιτο (12.7–8) | "so that for them … it might protect" | "so that the wall might protect for them the swift ships and the plentiful spoil it held within" | "keep safe", "guard", "save"; ῥύομαι "protect" |
| ληΐδα πολλήν (12.7) | "the plentiful spoil" | "the plentiful spoil" | "booty" (turned down at 13.262), "plunder", "loot"; ληΐς "spoil" as in the Odyssey table |
| θεῶν δ’ ἀέκητι τέτυκτο ἀθανάτων (12.8–9) | "against the will of the gods it had been made, the immortals’" | "against the will of the immortal gods" | "without the consent of", "in spite of"; ἀέκητι "against the will of" as in the table's 12.290 / 11.667 rows |
| ὄφρα μὲν … τόφρα δὲ (12.10–12) | "As long as … so long" | "As long as … so long" | "while … so long", "until"; the paired form is kept |
| μήνι’ (12.10) | "was wrathful" | "kept up his wrath" | "raged", "was angry" (χόλος keeps "anger"); μηνίω keeps "wrath" of μῆνις |
| Πριάμοιο ἄνακτος … πόλις (12.11) | "of Priam the lord … the city" | "the city of lord Priam" | "King Priam", "the king"; ἄναξ "lord" |
| ἀπόρθητος (12.11) | "unsacked" | "unsacked" | "unravaged", "unharmed", "untouched"; α-privative of πέρθω "sack" (πέρθετο "was sacked", 12.15) |
| ἔπλεν = ἔπλετο (12.11) | "was" | "was" | "proved", "turned out to be" |
| κατὰ … θάνον ὅσσοι ἄριστοι (12.13) | "had died all who were best" | "all the best … had died" | "the noblest", "the finest"; follows the table's ὅσσοι ἄριστοι "all the best men" (4.211–212) |
| οἳ μὲν δάμεν, οἳ δὲ λίποντο (12.14) | "some were overcome, and some were left" | "some overcome and some left" | "some fell, some survived" (each decides the sense); δάμνημι "overcome" as in the table's δουρὶ δαμέντες |
| δεκάτῳ ἐνιαυτῷ (12.15) | "in the tenth year" | "in the tenth year" | "ten years on", "after ten years" |
| φίλην ἐς πατρίδ’ (12.16) | "to their dear fatherland" | "to their dear fatherland" | "to their own land", "home" (drops φίλην); the table's φίλην ἐς πατρίδα γαῖαν with γαῖαν left out |
| μητιόωντο … ἀμαλδῦναι (12.17–18) | "devised … to wipe out" | "planned to wipe out" | "plotted", "resolved", "destroy" (reserved for ὄλλυμι), "obliterate"; ἀμαλδύνω "wipe out" is given in the same wording at 12.18 and 12.32 |
| ποταμῶν μένος (12.18) | "the might of the rivers" | "the might of the rivers" | "the strength of the rivers" (σθένος), "force", "fury"; μένος keeps the Iliad's "might" |
| ἅλα δὲ προρέουσι (12.19) | "to the sea flow forth" | "flow forth to the sea" | "into the sea"; ἅλα δέ read as ἅλαδε, as at 5.598 |
| ὄρη Ἰδαῖα (12.19) | "the Idaean mountains" | "the mountains of Ida" | "Mount Ida" (the plural ὄρεα is kept) |
| δῖος Σκάμανδρος (12.21) | "heavenly Scamander" | "heavenly Scamander" | "divine", "noble"; the table's δῖος "heavenly" |
| Σιμόεις (12.22) | "the Simois" | "the Simois" | "Simoeis"; the table's 5.774 row |
| βοάγρια (12.22) | "ox-hide shields" | "ox-hide shields" (+ note: meaning not known) | the table's 16.296 row, unchanged |
| τρυφάλειαι (12.22) | "helms" | "helmets" | the table's `l` "helm" / `i` "helmet" |
| ἡμιθέων γένος ἀνδρῶν (12.23) | "the race of men half-divine" | "the race of men who were half gods" | "demigods", "heroes" (ἥρως), "semi-divine"; ἡμίθεος "half-god" |
| ὁμόσε στόματ’ ἔτραπε (12.24) | "to the same place the mouths turned" | "turned the mouths of all of them to one place" | "directed the outlets"; στόμα "mouth" |
| ἐννῆμαρ … ἵει ῥόον (12.25) | "for nine days … he sent the flood" | "for nine days sent their flood" | "poured the torrent", "let the stream run"; ῥόος "stream, flow" (the table's ποταμός / "flowing" words) |
| ἁλίπλοα τείχεα (12.26; rare, sense uncertain) | "sea-sailed … the walls" | "sea-washed … the walls" (+ note: exact sense not certain) | "sea-swept", "ship-sailed" (each silently picks one guess), "floating"; ἅλς "sea" + πλέω "sail, float" |
| ἐννοσίγαιος (bare, of Poseidon, 12.27) | "the earth-shaker" | "the earth-shaker" | "Poseidon" (the Greek withholds the name here); the table's bare ἐννοσίγαιος (11.102) |
| ἔχων χείρεσσι τρίαιναν (12.27) | "holding in his hands the trident" | "holding the trident in his hands" | "wielding", "grasping" |
| θεμείλια … φιτρῶν καὶ λάων (12.28–29) | "the foundations … of logs and stones" | "the foundations, of logs and stones, which the Achaeans had laid with toil" | "beams", "boulders"; φιτρός "log" (the stem φυτ-), λᾶας "stone" |
| μογέοντες (12.29) | "toiling" | "with toil" | "labouring", "struggling" |
| λεῖα … ἐποίησεν (12.30) | "smooth he made" | "made them smooth" | "level", "flat" |
| ἀγάρροον Ἑλλήσποντον (12.30) | "strong-flowing Hellespont" | "strong-flowing Hellespont" | the table's ἀγάρροος (2.845), unchanged |
| ἠϊόνα μεγάλην ψαμάθοισι κάλυψε (12.31) | "the great beach with sands he covered" | "covered the great beach over again with sands" | the table's 7.462 row (καλύψαι) put into the aorist |
| κὰρ ῥόον (12.32–33) | "down the stream" | "down their stream" | "along the channel", "back into their course" |
| καλλίρροον ὕδωρ (12.33) | "fair-flowing water" | "fair-flowing water" | the table's καλλίρροος (17.206) |
| ὄπισθε … θησέμεναι (12.34–35) | "afterwards … to bring it about" | "in later days … to bring it about" | "to do", "to make" (no object); τίθημι "put, make" |
| ἐνοπή (12.35) | "shouting" | "shouting" | "din", "clamour" (κλαγγή); the table's 3.2 row |
| δεδήει (12.35) | "was ablaze" | "blazed" | "was kindled", "raged"; pluperfect of δαίω with the imperfect's sense |
| ἐΰδμητον τεῖχος (12.36) | "the well-built wall" | "the well-built wall" | the table's ἐΰδμητος (1.448) |
| δούρατα πύργων (12.36) | "the timbers of the towers" | "the timbers of its towers" | "spears", "beams" (the sense is wood, said in the note) |
| Διὸς μάστιγι δαμέντες (12.37) | "by the whip of Zeus overcome" | "overcome by the whip of Zeus" | "scourge", "lash"; μάστιξ "whip" (5.840) |
| νηυσὶν ἔπι γλαφυρῇσιν ἐελμένοι (12.38) | "at the hollow ships hemmed in" | "hemmed in at the hollow ships" | "penned", "cooped up", "shut in"; εἴλω "pen in, hem in" |
| ἰσχανόωντο (12.38) | "held themselves back" | "held themselves back" | "hung back", "cowered", "were held back" |
| δειδιότες (12.39) | "fearing" | "in fear of" | "dreading", "afraid of" |
| κρατερὸν μήστωρα φόβοιο (12.39) | "strong counsellor of flight" | "strong master of flight" | "mighty", "stout" (reserved for ἴφθιμος / στιβαρός); the table's μήστωρε φόβοιο (5.272) with κρατερός "strong" |
| ἶσος ἀέλλῃ (12.40) | "equal to a blast" | "like a storm" | "like a gale", "like a whirlwind"; the table's ἄελλα "blast" / "storm" |
| κάπριος ἠὲ λέων στρέφεται σθένεϊ βλεμεαίνων (12.42) | "a boar or a lion wheels, in strength exulting" | "a boar or a lion wheels about, exulting in its strength" (+ note: βλεμεαίνων uncertain) | "revelling in", "proud of" (each decides the open sense); σθένος "strength" |
| πυργηδὸν σφέας αὐτοὺς ἀρτύναντες (12.43) | "tower-wise themselves having arrayed" | "array themselves like a tower" | "in a tower-like mass", "in a wall"; πύργος "tower", the table's note that it is a close-packed body of men |
| θαμειὰς αἰχμάς (12.44–45) | "thickset spears" | "spear after spear … in close succession" | "volleys", "showers", "javelins"; αἰχμή "spear" |
| κυδάλιμον κῆρ (12.45) | "the glorious heart" | "the glorious heart" | "famous", "noble"; κυδάλιμος "glorious" (the table's 4.403 row) |
| ταρβεῖ οὐδὲ φοβεῖται (12.46) | "is dismayed nor takes flight" | "is never dismayed and never takes flight" | "fears nor fears", "is afraid"; two different words, kept apart |
| ἀγηνορίη (12.46) | "manliness" | "manliness" (+ note: praise or blame) | "courage", "pride", "arrogance", "valour" (each picks one side of the word) |
| ἔκτα (12.46, general statement) | "kills" | "kills" | "killed", "has killed" |
| ταρφέα (12.47) | "often" | "again and again" | "thickly", "swiftly" |
| στίχας ἀνδρῶν (12.47, 12.48) | "the ranks of men" | "the ranks of men" | "lines of men"; στίχες "ranks" (the table's 3.196 / 5.166 rows) |
| ἐλλίσσεθ’ ἑταίρους (12.49) | "begged his companions" | "begging his companions" | "entreated", "pleaded with"; ἑταῖρος "companion" |
| ὠκύποδες ἵπποι (12.51) | "the swift-footed" (horses) | "swift-footed horses" | "fleet-footed"; the table's ὠκύποδες |
| ἐπ’ ἄκρῳ χείλει ἐφεσταότες (12.51–52) | "on the topmost lip, standing upon it" | "on the very edge" | "brim", "rim"; χεῖλος "lip, edge" |
| ἀπὸ … δειδίσσετο τάφρος (12.52) | "scared them off the ditch" | "the ditch scared them off" | "frightened them back", "put them in dread"; the middle with an active sense |
| ὑπερθορέειν σχεδὸν … περῆσαι ῥηϊδίη (12.53–54) | "neither to leap over from near nor to cross easy" | "neither easy to leap across from close by nor easy to cross" | "to jump", "to pass"; the two verbs kept apart |
| κρημνοὶ ἐπηρεφέες (12.54) | "banks, overhanging" | "overhanging banks" | "cliffs", "crags", "steep sides"; κρημνός "steep bank" |
| σκόλοπες ὀξέες (12.55–56, 12.63–64) | "stakes sharp" | "sharp stakes" | "spikes", "palisades", "pales"; σκόλοψ "stake" |
| υἷες Ἀχαιῶν (12.56) | "the sons of the Achaeans" | "the sons of the Achaeans" | "the Achaean youths"; the stock phrase kept |
| δηΐων ἀνδρῶν ἀλεωρήν (12.57) | "a defence from hostile men" | "a defence against enemy men" | "ward", "protection" (kept for ἀλκή / ἄλκαρ "defence"); δήϊος "hostile" |
| ἐΰτροχον ἅρμα τιταίνων (12.58) | "a well-rolling chariot straining at" | "straining at a well-rolling chariot" | "pulling", "drawing"; the table's ἐΰτροχος and τιταίνων |
| μενοίνεον εἰ τελέουσι (12.59) | "were eager if they would accomplish it" | "were eager to see whether they would manage it" | "were minded to try", "hoped"; μενοινάω "be eager, be minded"; "to see" is supplied in `i` only |
| θρασὺν Ἕκτορα (12.60) | "bold Hector" | "bold Hector" | "daring", "brave", "rash"; the table's θρασύς "bold" |
| εἶπε παραστάς (12.60) | "spoke, standing beside him" | "stood beside … and spoke" | the table's εἶπε παραστάς (6.75) |
| Τρώων ἀγοὶ ἠδ’ ἐπικούρων (12.61) | "leaders of the Trojans and of the allies" | "leaders of the Trojans and of the allies" | "captains", "chiefs", "helpers"; ἀγός "leader", ἐπίκουρος "ally" |
| ἀφραδέως (12.62) | "senselessly" | "senselessly" | "foolishly" (reserved for νήπιος), "rashly"; the table's ἀφραδέως (3.436) |
| ἀργαλέη περάαν (12.63) | "very hard to cross" | "very hard to cross" | "difficult", "dangerous"; ἀργαλέος "hard" |
| καταβήμεναι οὐδὲ μάχεσθαι ἱππεῦσι (12.65–66) | "to go down or to fight for horsemen" | "for horsemen to go down or to fight" | "charioteers" (kept for ἡνίοχοι), "riders"; ἱππεύς "horseman" |
| στεῖνος (12.66) | "a narrow place" | "a narrow place" | "narrows", "a tight spot"; the table's στεῖνος "narrow place" (8.476) |
| τρώσεσθαι ὀΐω (12.66) | "where I think we shall be wounded" | "there, I think, we shall be wounded" | "I suspect", "I fear"; ὀΐω "I think" as in iliad-001 to -003 and 11.609 |
| κακὰ φρονέων … ἀλαπάζει (12.67) | "evils devising … is laying waste" | "with evil in his mind … is laying … waste" | "plundering", "sacking"; ἀλαπάζω "lay waste" (the table's 2.367) |
| Ζεὺς ὑψιβρεμέτης (12.68) | "Zeus the high-thundering" | "Zeus who thunders on high" | "loud-thundering", "far-thundering" (εὐρύοπα); the table's ὑψιβρεμέτης (5.4) |
| Τρώεσσι δὲ ἵετ’ ἀρήγειν (12.68) | "for the Trojans is eager to help" | "is eager to help the Trojans" | "is bent on helping", "longs to"; ἵεμαι "be eager" |
| ἦ τ’ ἂν ἔγωγ’ ἐθέλοιμι (12.69) | "then indeed I for my part would wish" | "then I for one would wish" | "I would be glad", "I would prefer"; ἐθέλω "wish, be willing" |
| νωνύμνους ἀπολέσθαι ἀπ’ Ἄργεος (12.70) | "nameless to perish far from Argos" | "perish here, nameless, far from Argos" | "without glory", "inglorious", "unknown"; νώνυμνος "nameless" |
| ὑποστρέψωσι (12.71) | "they turn about" | "they turn around" | "wheel", "retreat"; the Achaeans are the subject |
| παλίωξις (12.71; rare) | "a chase back" | "a chase back from the ships" (+ note: sense not exactly known) | "counter-charge", "rout", "pursuit" (each silently picks one guess) |
| τάφρῳ ἐνιπλήξωμεν ὀρυκτῇ (12.72) | "into the ditch we dash, the dug one" | "we dash into the dug ditch" | "crash", "tumble"; the table's τάφρον ὀρυκτήν "the dug ditch" (9.67) |
| οὐδ’ ἄγγελον ἀπονέεσθαι (12.73) | "not even a messenger will go back" | "not even a messenger will get back" | "no news", "a single messenger"; ἄγγελος "messenger" (the table) |
| ἄστυ (12.74) | "the town" | "the town" | "city" (reserved for πόλις); the table's ἄστυ "town" (2.801) |
| ἑλιχθέντων ὑπ’ Ἀχαιῶν (12.74) | "having been wheeled round by the Achaeans" | "when we have been turned about by the Achaeans" | "routed", "driven back"; ἑλίσσω "turn, wheel" |
| ἵππους μὲν θεράποντες ἐρυκόντων (12.76) | "the horses, let the attendants hold back" | "let the attendants hold the horses back" | "servants" (reserved for δμῶες), "grooms"; θεράπων "attendant" |
| αὐτοὶ δὲ πρυλέες σὺν τεύχεσι θωρηχθέντες (12.77) | "ourselves, the foot-soldiers, with our armour armed" | "let us ourselves, the foot-soldiers, armed in our armour" | the published 12.77 wording with the person changed (they to we), and "let us" carried over from the verb before it; "rushed" belongs to the other unit |
| ἑπώμεθ’ ἀολλέες (12.78) | "let us follow, in a close mass" | "follow … in a close mass" | "massed together", "in a body", "in a throng", "all together" (reserved for ἅμα / ἀθρόοι); the table's ἀολλέες "in a close mass" (5.498) |
| οὐ μενέουσ’ (12.79) | "will not stand" | "will not stand their ground" | "will not wait", "will not hold out" (kept for σχήσειν) |
| ὀλέθρου πείρατ’ ἐφῆπται (12.79) | "upon them the limits of destruction have been fastened" | "the limits of destruction have indeed been fastened upon them" | the table's 7.402 row, unchanged |
| ὣς φάτο Πουλυδάμας (12.80, whole-half-line closing formula) | "So spoke Polydamas" | "So spoke Polydamas" | "Thus Polydamas said"; the table's ὣς φάτο / ὣς ἔφατ’ rows |
| ἅδε δ’ Ἕκτορι μῦθος ἀπήμων (12.80) | "it pleased Hector, the word, harmless" | "his harmless word pleased Hector" | "sound", "safe", "good" (each loses the negative of ἀ-πῆμα), "unharmed" (kept for persons); ἁνδάνω "please", ἀπήμων "harmless" as of the wind (5.268) |
| οὐδὲ μὲν ἄλλοι Τρῶες ἐφ’ ἵππων ἠγερέθοντο (12.82) | "were gathering on their horses" | "stay massed on their horses" | "stay mounted", "stay in their chariots" (each picks one reading); ἀγερέθομαι "gather" |
| ἀλλ’ ἀπὸ πάντες ὄρουσαν (12.83) | "off all leapt" | "they all leapt down" | "sprang", "dismounted"; ὀρούω "leap, rush" |
| Ἕκτορα δῖον (12.83) | "Hector, the heavenly" | "heavenly Hector" | "noble", "godlike" (ἀντίθεος); the table's δῖος "heavenly" |
| διαστάντες … πένταχα κοσμηθέντες (12.86–87) | "having stood apart … in five parts set in order" | "standing apart … set in order in five divisions" | "five columns", "five companies" (the Greek says only "in five ways"); κοσμέω "set in order" |
| ἅμ’ ἡγεμόνεσσιν ἕποντο (12.87) | "together with the leaders followed" | "followed along with their leaders" | "commanders" (ἀρχός), "guides"; ἡγεμών "leader" |

No departure from an Odyssey rendering was made. Lines 12.6 (as 7.450 in the table), 12.75, 12.77, 12.81, 12.84 and 12.85 take the published English as far as each sentence allows; 12.80–81 form one unit, so their English is the published one set in the longer sentence.
